features.name: Bandipora & Wular Lake

features.fact: Cloudbursts in Bandipora swelled the Jhelum and Wular Lake, putting lakeside villages near the flood mark on alert.
features.locate: North Kashmir in the Jhelum valley, beneath Harmukh peak.

features.name: Chamba

features.locate: Western Himalaya on the Ravi river between the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges.

features.name: Amrabad Tiger Reserve
features.fact: Preliminary 2026 census data reported a rise in the reserve's tiger population around International Tiger Day.

features.locate: Island and inland African locations spanning the Mozambique Channel, Gulf of Guinea and White Nile/Sudd.

features.locate: The Lifou–Maré–Ouvéa island chain east of New Caledonia in the Coral Sea.

features.locate: Western Himalaya, near Dharamshala in the Beas river basin below the Dhauladhar range.

features.locate: On the Arabian Sea, near the southern tip of India south of Thiruvananthapuram.

features.name: Changthang & Karakoram Sanctuaries

features.locate: High cold-desert plateau of eastern Ladakh and northern Siachen-Karakoram belt.

features.locate: Southern edge of Kaziranga between Brahmaputra floodplain and Karbi Anglong hills.

features.locate: Andreanof group in central Aleutian Islands between the Bering Sea and North Pacific.

features.locate: Jabal al-Druze plateau near the Jordan border, southeast of Daraa and Golan Heights.

features.locate: Eastern coast of China along the East China Sea and Yellow Sea.

features.locate: Central Spain near Madrid, extending across the northern Mediterranean fire belt.

features.locate: Chokepoint splitting Red Sea and Gulf of Aden via Perim/Mayyun Island.

features.locate: North Sikkim, between the Teesta valley and the Kanchenjunga massif.

features.locate: Eastern Meghalaya on the Shillong plateau; the Myntdu drains towards Bangladesh.

features.locate: North of Imphal in the Sadar Hills, across the Imphal–Dimapur corridor.

features.locate: Reached by the Pahalgam route through Sheshnag or the shorter Baltal route.

features.locate: At Munirabad near Hosapete and Hampi.

features.locate: Nathu La overlooks Chumbi Valley; Shipki La is where the Sutlej enters India.

features.locate: Trans-Himalayan Kailash range, near the sources of the Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra and Karnali.

features.locate: Albay province in southern Luzon, overlooking Legazpi City.

features.name: Surha Tal

features.locate: Ballia district in far-eastern Uttar Pradesh near Bihar.

features.name: Kaziranga National Park

features.locate: On the Brahmaputra's south bank with the Karbi Anglong hills to the south.

features.name: Western Ghats / Kerala

features.locate: Parallel to India's southwest coast, separating the coastal plain from the Deccan.

features.locate: Narrow west-coast belt between the Arabian Sea and the Sahyadri.

features.locate: Mundra is on the Gulf of Kachchh; Nhava Sheva lies across Mumbai harbour.

features.locate: High-altitude frontier east of Leh along the Line of Actual Control.

features.name: Évian-les-Bains

features.locate: Haute-Savoie, directly across the lake from Switzerland.

features.name: Strait of Hormuz

features.locate: Between Iran and Musandam, linking the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

features.name: Gulf of Aden & Bab-el-Mandeb

features.name: Kīlauea
features.fact: A new eruptive episode produced exceptional lava fountains.
features.locate: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island.

features.name: Kanlaon Volcano
features.fact: Ongoing eruptions underlined the Philippines' tectonic setting.
features.locate: Central Visayas between Panay and Cebu.

features.name: Valmikinagar / Gandak
features.fact: after the Aug 26 Himalayan glacier-collapse flood in Nepal, all 36 gates of the Gandak barrage were opened and 8 Bihar districts — Gopalganj, Saran (Chapra), West Champaran (Bettiah), East Champaran (Motihari), Muzaffarpur, Vaishali, Sitamarhi, Sheohar — were put on alert with NDRF deployed and low-lying areas evacuated. UP and Uttarakhand also evacuated riverside pockets.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Valmikinagar Barrage & the Gandak plain — West Champaran, Bihar. On the Gandak (Narayani) where it leaves Nepal and enters India at the Indo-Nepal border in West Champaran district, at the western edge of the north-Bihar plains; Valmiki Tiger Reserve and the Someshwar (Shivalik) hills lie immediately north, the Ganga confluence at Sonepur/Hajipur far downstream.

features.name: Kaziranga
features.fact: on Aug 24 the Central Empowered Committee censured Assam for failing to enforce the Supreme Court's 2019 ban on mining in the catchments of streams rising in Karbi Anglong; the same SC bench ordered a fresh nationwide survey of elephant corridors and barred fireballs/spikes used to divert elephants.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kaziranga National Park & the Karbi Anglong hills — Assam. In the Brahmaputra floodplain of central Assam, spanning Golaghat and Nagaon districts; the Karbi Anglong plateau forms its southern boundary (elephants cross between the two in flood season), Jorhat to the east, the Eastern Himalaya beyond the river to the north. A UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985) and Tiger Reserve (2006), holding the world's largest one-horned rhino population.

features.name: Khalingduar / Udalguri region
features.fact: an Aaranyak project reported this week converts three invasive alien plants — Lantana camara, Chromolaena odorata (Siam weed) and Mikania micrantha — into biochar to restore native elephant forage.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Khalingduar Reserve Forest, Udalguri — Assam (Bodoland Territorial Region). Northern Assam in the Bodoland Territorial Region, on the Bhutan border at the foot of the eastern Himalayan duars, in the Dhansiri forest division north of the Brahmaputra.

features.name: Singhbhum Craton region
features.fact: a PNAS paper (reported Aug 24) dated a banded chert at Bhitardari to ~3.5 billion years using zircon U-Pb, making it the oldest directly dated rock carrying a confirmed biosignature of microbial life.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Bhitardari & the Singhbhum Craton — Jharkhand / Odisha. The Singhbhum craton is the ancient stable block of the Chota Nagpur–north Odisha shield, roughly between the Subarnarekha and the Baitarani, taking in Jharkhand's Singhbhum copper belt and northern Odisha (Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar).

features.name: Domiasiat / Khasi Hills region
features.fact: on Aug 26 the Meghalaya Assembly unanimously passed a resolution against all uranium mining and processing in the state, asking the Centre to shut the Kylleng-Pyndengsohiong Mawthabah (KPM) project — Domiasiat holds one of India's richest uranium deposits.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Domiasiat & the West Khasi Hills — Meghalaya. On the Meghalaya (Shillong) plateau west of Shillong, in West Khasi Hills / South West Khasi Hills districts, on the rain-drenched southern slope facing the Bangladesh plains (Wahkyn and Lostoin lie nearby).

features.name: Paradip Port
features.fact: seven projects were commissioned here on Aug 21 (including deepening to 18.5 m), and on Aug 28 a 30-year concession was awarded to mechanise the CQ-III berth.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Paradip Port — Jagatsinghpur district, Odisha. On the Bay of Bengal at the mouth of the Mahanadi delta (near the Jatadhari and Mahanadi estuaries), north of the Devi river mouth and south of Dhamra; a major deep-draught eastern port.

features.name: Rasuwa / Trishuli valley
features.fact: on Aug 26 an ice-rock avalanche off a glacier at ~5,200 m dammed the Lhende; the burst sent a surge that raised the Trishuli 9 m in 30 minutes — 389+ dead in Nepal, 1,500+ missing across Nepal and Tibet, 19 bridges and ~40 km of road gone. The landslide itself registered as a magnitude-5.2 seismic event (not an earthquake trigger, per USGS).
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Rasuwa district & the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli system — Nepal. Central Nepal directly north of Kathmandu, on the Tibet (China) border; Timure and Syapru Besi sit in the Lhende Khola / Bhote Koshi valley, which becomes the Trishuli, flows through Nuwakot and Dhading, joins the Narayani, and crosses into Bihar as the Gandak. Langtang National Park frames the valley.

features.name: Gyirong border crossing
features.fact: mud and debris from the same Aug 26 flood struck Gyirong Port; 558 missing (260 foreign nationals, many Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims). Premier Li Qiang visited, and Xi Jinping ordered an "all-out" search.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Gyirong (Kyirong) County & Gyirong Port — Shigatse, Tibet, China. On the southern rim of the Tibetan Plateau in Shigatse prefecture, the main China–Nepal land trade gateway west of the older Kodari/Zhangmu crossing, on the road toward Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar.

features.name: Tashkent
features.fact: PM Modi's state visit on Aug 29–30, 2026 (his fourth), with delegation-level talks with President Mirziyoyev.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Tashkent — Uzbekistan. Capital of Uzbekistan in the Chirchik valley at the western end of the Fergana/Tian Shan foothills, in the Amu Darya–Syr Darya (Turan) basin of doubly-landlocked Central Asia; Kazakhstan lies north, the Kyzylkum desert west.

features.name: Bishkek
features.fact: hosts the 26th SCO Summit, Aug 31–Sep 1, 2026, marking the bloc's 25th anniversary — agenda includes an SCO development bank and the flagship China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan (CKU) railway.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Bishkek — Kyrgyzstan. Capital in the Chuy valley at the northern foot of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too (Tian Shan), near the Kazakh border; Lake Issyk-Kul lies east, the Fergana valley south-west.

features.name: Torugart Pass
features.fact: the flagship connectivity project of the Bishkek SCO summit; note the gauge break at Makmal (1,435 mm Chinese standard → 1,520 mm Russian broad gauge).
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Torugart Pass & the CKU railway corridor — China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan. A Tian Shan pass on the China–Kyrgyzstan border; the ~530 km line runs Kashgar → Torugart → Makmal → Jalal-Abad → Andijan, threading the Tian Shan (Naryn, Kosh-Dobo and Fergana tunnels) into the Fergana valley, and feeds the Middle Corridor toward the Caspian and Türkiye.

features.name: Kaub / Rhine
features.fact: Europe's drought-hit summer pushed all four to record lows — Kaub fell to 21 cm on Aug 3–4, the lowest since records began in 1880 — stalling Rhine barge traffic into late August and straining cooling water at the Paks nuclear plant.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kaub on the Rhine — with the Danube at Paks, the Po at Cremona, the Loire at Saumur. Kaub is the Rhine's shallowest reference gauge, in the Rhine gorge between Bingen and Koblenz, Germany; Paks is on the middle Danube in Hungary; Cremona on the Po in the north-Italian plain; Saumur on the Loire, France's longest river.

features.name: Kīlauea
features.fact: Episode 54 of the episodic Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ran through Aug 25, with lava fountains to ~150 m (500 ft) over nine hours before pausing.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kīlauea & Halemaʻumaʻu crater — Hawaiʻi Island, USA. A shield volcano on the southeast flank of Hawaiʻi (Big Island), beside Mauna Loa, on the Hawaiian hotspot in the mid-Pacific — a classic intra-plate / hotspot volcano, not on the Ring of Fire.

features.name: Surat Thani
features.fact: Exercise Maitree 2026 (India–Thailand jungle/counter-insurgency) ran Aug 18–31 at Vibhavadi Rangsit Camp, Surat Thani; Exercise Udara Shakti 2026 (India–Malaysia air) was held at Subang from Aug 13.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Surat Thani — Thailand (with Subang, Malaysia). Surat Thani lies on the Gulf of Thailand coast of the Malay Peninsula, near the Isthmus of Kra and opposite Ko Samui; Subang air base sits near Kuala Lumpur on the peninsula's western, Strait of Malacca side.

features.name: Palampet / Ramappa
features.fact: on Aug 31 the Centre/ASI notified the Kakatiya-era Gollala Gudi — a trikutalaya (three-shrine) temple beside Ramappa — as a Monument of National Importance under the AMASR Act, 1958.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Gollala Gudi, Palampet — Mulugu district, Telangana. Palampet lies in northeastern Telangana on the Deccan plateau, in the Godavari basin north-east of Warangal (Mulugu was carved out of Warangal in 2019); it already hosts the Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2021.

features.name: Sriharikota
features.fact: ISRO flew GSLV-F17 with EOS-05 at 02:55 IST on Sep 4, placing the 2,367-kg satellite — the GSLV's heaviest payload yet — into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Sriharikota & the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) — Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh. A barrier island on the Bay of Bengal that separates Pulicat Lake (India's second-largest brackish lagoon, shared with Tamil Nadu) from the sea, roughly 80 km north of Chennai; the spindle-shaped island gives an eastward over-sea launch corridor and sits close to the equator.

features.name: Prayagraj / Sangam
features.fact: around Sep 1 both rivers rose sharply after torrential rain over Uttarakhand and western UP, pushing floodwater into riverbank settlements at Prayagraj and putting Ganga–Yamuna danger marks under watch.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Prayagraj (Sangam of Ganga & Yamuna) — Uttar Pradesh. At the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganga and the Yamuna in the southern Doab; upstream the Yamuna passes Delhi–Agra–Etawah, the Ganga passes Kanpur; downstream the combined river runs to Varanasi and the Ghaghara/Son junctions.

features.name: Pakal Dul / Marusudar
features.fact: the 1,000 MW Pakal Dul project (CVPPL/NHPC) — which will carry India's tallest dam on the Indus system (167 m) — is being pushed to commissioning through September–December 2026, part of the accelerated Chenab build-out after the Indus Waters Treaty was put in abeyance.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Pakal Dul dam & the Marusudar river — Kishtwar district, Jammu & Kashmir. On the Marusudar, the largest tributary of the Chenab, in the Chenab valley between the Pir Panjal and the Great Himalaya; Kishtwar lies east of Doda, with the Kiru, Kwar and Ratle projects on the same stretch.

features.name: Vizhinjam
features.fact: India's first deepwater transshipment port began full EXIM (export–import) operations from Aug 18, reviewed again in late August; Kerala simultaneously launched "Mission Samudra", a port-led plan for a Vizhinjam Maritime Economic Region along the state's 600-km coast — a direct challenge to Colombo, Singapore and Jebel Ali.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Vizhinjam (Thiruvananthapuram) — Kerala. On the Arabian Sea/Malabar coast about 16 km south of Thiruvananthapuram, next to Kovalam and close to Cape Comorin (Kanniyakumari); it sits ~10 nautical miles off the east–west international shipping lane, with a natural depth of ~20 m.

features.name: Bharat Mandapam / Delhi
features.fact: India, chairing BRICS in 2026 under the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," will host the 18th BRICS Summit here on Sep 12–13 — announcements and sherpa-level preparation ran through the first week of September.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan — New Delhi. On the Yamuna's right bank in the National Capital Territory, the venue that hosted the 2023 G20 summit.

features.name: Kargil–Leh corridor (Kargil anchor)
features.fact: a fortnight-long "Ladakh Peace and Justice March" from Kargil to Leh was announced in late August for Sep 10–24, timed to the first anniversary of the 2025 Leh firing, reviving the demand for statehood and Sixth Schedule status for Ladakh.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kargil → Leh, Ladakh (UT). Kargil sits on the Suru river (an Indus tributary) in the trans-Himalayan Zanskar range, linked to the Kashmir valley by the Zoji La pass; Leh lies downstream on the Indus itself, below the Ladakh range and the Khardung La.

features.name: Zhangpu / Taiwan Strait coast
features.fact: Typhoon Saudel, the 18th storm of the 2026 Pacific season, made a rare third landfall at Zhangpu on Sep 3 after two landfalls at Yuhuan on Aug 28; 83,000+ were evacuated in Fujian and more than 100 houses collapsed at Huating, Putian.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Zhangpu (Zhangzhou), Fujian — with Yuhuan, Zhejiang, China. Zhangpu is on Fujian's south coast facing the Taiwan Strait, near Xiamen; Putian lies up the same coast; Yuhuan is an island-county of Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the East China Sea.

features.name: Johnson Bayou
features.fact: Tropical Storm Edouard came ashore here on Sep 1 with 60 mph winds, then stalled over east Texas and dumped 10–21 inches of rain, knocking out power to 150,000+ customers.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Johnson Bayou (Cameron Parish), Louisiana — USA. On the Gulf of Mexico coast right at the Texas–Louisiana line, beside Sabine Pass and Sabine Lake, west of the Atchafalaya basin and east of Galveston Bay.

features.name: Anak Krakatau
features.fact: a major eruption at 00:50 WIB on Sep 5 threw ash to about 15 km (50,000 ft), tracked west by the Darwin VAAC — a live aviation and tsunami-risk concern on one of the world's busiest sea lanes.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Anak Krakatau & the Sunda Strait — Indonesia. The "child of Krakatoa" cone in the Sunda Strait, the channel separating Sumatra from Java and linking the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean; the 1883 caldera collapse and the 1927 rebirth of the cone happened here.

features.name: Mount Sinabung
features.fact: Indonesia's Geological Agency raised Sinabung to Level III (Siaga) after an Aug 31 eruption sent ash ~3,500 m above the summit — its first serious reactivation in several years.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Mount Sinabung — Karo, North Sumatra, Indonesia. A stratovolcano in the Barisan range of northern Sumatra, close to Lake Toba (the world's largest volcanic lake) and the Toba caldera, inland of Medan.

features.name: Natanz region
features.fact: on Sep 5 the US president said Washington might "hit" the site "very soon" — the deeply buried (100 m+) hall that the IAEA has never been allowed to inspect — as US–Iran strikes continued through early September.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La ("Pickaxe Mountain") & Natanz — Isfahan province, Iran. On Iran's arid Central Plateau, ~225 km south of Tehran, immediately south of the Natanz enrichment complex and north of Isfahan, in the shadow of the Zagros.

features.name: Niamey / Niger
features.fact: on the night of Aug 28–29 mutinous junior officers — reportedly drawn from the jihadist-hit Dosso, Téra and Tillabéri regions — seized the airport, state radio and TV in a coup attempt; the Presidential Guard, with Russian backing, retook Base 101, and the junta declared the plot foiled.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Niamey & Base 101 — Niger (with the Tillabéri, Téra and Dosso regions). Niamey stands on the Niger river in south-western Niger; Base 101 adjoins Diori Hamani airport. Tillabéri covers the Liptako-Gourma tri-border with Mali and Burkina Faso (Téra and Ouallam within it); Dosso lies south toward the Benin/Nigeria frontier.

features.name: Kyiv / Dnieper corridor
features.fact: Sep 1–2 brought a sixth consecutive night of mass Russian missile-and-drone strikes, killing at least a dozen in Kyiv (seven of them at a railway depot) and hitting Odesa and Dnipro as the school year opened.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Kyiv, Odesa and Dnipro — Ukraine. Kyiv on the Dnieper (Dnipro) in the north; Dnipro city downstream in the industrial east; Odesa the Black Sea port near the Dniester estuary and the Danube delta.
